claims_disputed.claim: Joint planning (not just planning) is the source of the gain: +3.3 to +8.3 pp over implementation-only planning.
claims_disputed.reason: Table 3 is one backend (Opus-4.7) with one run per cell. Plan-Seq 'runs the program-then-proof pipeline' (§5.1), while P3's skill also carries an external plan-gate verifier subagent, an instruction-compliance verifier subagent, per-target edit/tactic caps and pivot rules (App. E). The ablation therefore does not isolate joint planning from the rest of the skill. The AlgoVeri Plan-Seq cell (44.8%) cannot be obtained with n=77 (34/77=44.2, 35/77=45.5).

pattern_stance_changes.reason: All arms (Plain, Seq, Plan-Seq, P3) do Lean-verified generation with the same checker (§5.1). Formal verification is the shared setting, not a variable, so the paper gives no evidence for or against using formal methods compared with an alternative.
Every arm receives the same formal spec plus the same added algorithmic instruction (§5.1). Spec-first is never varied; the review's note is an inference ('result implies'), not a measurement.

Lean-feedback repair runs in every arm and is never ablated. The Appendix K restart data, if anything, show that the patch-and-retry loop alone is costly. Most Table 6 percentages cannot be obtained as k/n for one run per task (e.g. Verina 11.7, 24.2, 7.8 of 189; nearly all AlgoVeri cells of 77), so that evidence is unreliable as reported.

missed_issues: Numerical inconsistency: with one run per task (§5.1), 9 of 12 Verina, 11 of 12 AlgoVeri and 10 of 12 Lean4Commit0 full-restart rates in Table 6, and the Table 3 AlgoVeri Plan-Seq cell, cannot be obtained from the stated task counts. Table 2 values are all consistent. The trace-labeling method for 'full restart' is also not described (App. K).

Bundle confound: P3 is a six-phase skill with exit gates, LLM verifier subagents (lean_plan_verify, lean-verifier-instruction), hard edit caps and optional cheaper-subagent dispatch (App. E). The gain is attributed to 'joint planning', but a static gated workflow (P36) is what is really compared. This fits P36 better than P13 alone and is worth noting in the KB.

The scoring rule says a task is solved only if it 'satisfies the instruction' (Table 2 caption), but the paper does not say who or what judges instruction compliance. P3 has its own instruction-compliance gate (App. E Phase 6), so it may be optimised for the evaluation criterion; the baselines' gates are not described.

Efficiency on the solved intersection (App. L, Table 7) is mixed rather than 'broadly comparable'. P3 is slower or costlier in several cells, e.g. AlgoVeri Opus-4.7 $2.86/36.9 min vs Seq $2.31/26.6 min, and Lean4Commit0 Codex time 18.4 vs Plain 14.2.
Plan-retention and failure attribution (App. I) cover only Verina with Opus-4.7 and are author-coded.

Reproducibility of 3 is slightly low: the figshare snapshot reportedly has the harness, prompts, benchmark, scripts, pinned environment and run metadata (§5.1, App. E), so it rates 4 under the rubric. The backends are closed.
note: I agree with admit_with_caveats and with P13 supports: there are consistent gains in 12 of 12 cells across four backends. The P35, P14 and P16 'supports' stances are inflated: they tag the shared experimental setting, which never varies, rather than a tested intervention. The ablation does not isolate joint planning from the rest of the gated skill. Some appendix percentages cannot be obtained from the stated task counts.
